title: Fiend
html:
For the Warlock subclass, see The Fiend.

Fiends are a type of creature that are from the Lower Planes. They are creatures born of pure evil.

“
Evil, wicked creatures from the Lower Planes that labour under the leadership of lawful archdevils or chaotic demon princes.
„
— In-game racial description

Characteristics

Fiends come in a variety of forms and sizes. Some are intelligent, while others are not. They are so long-lived that they have an unknown lifespan; as such they do not grow old. With the possible exceptions of  Shovel and  Haarlep, most fiends in the game are from the (nine) Hells, rather than the Abyss.[1]

Most fiend creatures are resistant or immune to ⁠Fire damage, due to coming from the Lower Planes.

Types of fiends

Cambion

Main articles: Cambion and  Cambion on the Forgotten Realms Wiki
“
Scarlet-eyed and bitter-tempered, cambion are the bastard children of devils and mortals, a fusion of two Planes in one body.
„
— In-game racial description

Cambion are half-humanoid half-fiend hybrids.

Cambions in Baldur's Gate 3

  •  Cirrus
  •  Feena
  •  Mizora
  •  Raphael
  •  Vengeful Cambion
  •  Zhalk

Devil

Main article:  Devil on the Forgotten Realms Wiki
“
Both lawful and evil to the bone, devils live to scheme and exploit the rules they follow, be it to climb the hierarchy of the Nine Hells or to lay claim to the souls of the mortals they make contracts with.
„
— In-game racial description

Devils are highly lawful fiends that believe in order. They differ greatly from demons, who believe only in chaos.

Devils in Baldur's Gate 3

  •  Raphael

In game data, there is no devil race. Raphael is defined as a Cambion instead.

Gnoll Flind

Main articles: Flind and  Flind on the Forgotten Realms Wiki
“
Feral, hyena-like humanoids that slaughter indiscriminately in an attempt to quell the insatiable hunger of their demonic creator, Yeenoghu.
„
— In-game racial description

Flinds are related to Gnolls, but are particularly strong and vicious and part-fiend themselves

Gnoll Flinds in Baldur's Gate 3

  •  Flind

Hellsboar

Main articles: Hellsboar and  Hellsboar on the Forgotten Realms Wiki
“
Grafted with infernal iron and burning with hellfire, these porcine brutes are filled with a distinct brand of malice.
„
— In-game racial description

Hellsboar are fiends that look like large boars, with large boney skulls.

Hellsboars in Baldur's Gate 3

  •  Gilded Hellsboar
  •  Lesser Hellsboar
  •  Vengeful Boar

The Vengeful Boar is defined as its own race in game data, making it technically not a hellsboar.

Imp

Main articles: Imp and  Imp on the Forgotten Realms Wiki
“
Cackling peddlers of infernal mischief, imps bind themselves to the service of more powerful devils who furnish them with commands.
„
— In-game racial description

Imps are a small, manipulative fiends that serve their masters as foot soldiers or servants.

Imps in Baldur's Gate 3

  •  Cursed Imp
  •  Cruor
  •  Gilded Imp
  •  Lesser Imp
  •  Vengeful Imp

Merregon

Main articles: Merregon and  Merregon on the Forgotten Realms Wiki
“
In life, these faceless legionnaires of the Nine Hells were soldiers who served evil without reservation.
„
— In-game racial description

Merregon are the foot soldiers of the armies of most devils in the Nine Hells and live to serve their masters. They wear masks and can't speak, though they can form a sort of hive-mind when grouped together.

Merregons in Baldur's Gate 3

  •  Hoarding Merregon
  •  Merregon Legionnaire
  •  Vengeful Merregon

Succubus & Incubus

Main articles: Succubus & Incubus and  Succubus on the Forgotten Realms Wiki
“
Native to the Lower Planes, succubi beckon those they seduce with soft fingers, concealing their claws beneath.
„
— In-game racial description
“
Sensual and depraved, these dark-winged fiends from the Nine Hells derive pleasure from enticing and devouring lonely souls.
„
— In-game racial description

Succubi/Incubi are crafty demons whose purpose is to seduce and tempt mortals in order to take their souls.

Succubi / Incubi in Baldur's Gate 3

  •  Haarlep

Other fiends

The following types of fiend don't have their own data entry in the game. The listed creatures are defined directly as fiends by game data, not as any sub-type of it.

Orthon

Main article:  Orthon on the Forgotten Realms Wiki

Orthons are hulking humanoid fiends that serve as heavy infantry in the Nine Hells, fulfilling roles such as formation fighter, brutish berserker, and bounty hunter.

Orthons in Baldur's Gate 3

  •  Yurgir

Quasit

Main article: Quasit and  Quasit on the Forgotten Realms Wiki

Quasits are a chaotic race of fiend that embody wickedness and cruelty.

Quasits in Baldur's Gate 3

  •  Conjured Quasit
  •  Shovel

Related items

  • Hammer of the Just - additional 1d6⁠⁠Bludgeoning damage against fiends
  • Holy Water - deals 3d6⁠⁠Radiant damage against fiends
  • The Blood of Lathander - blinds nearby fiends
  • The Undead Bane - deals additional damage and applies  Bane to fiends
  • Voss' Silver Sword - +1d4 bonus to attack rolls and damage against fiends

Related spells and abilities

  • Aura of Hate - nearby fiends deal Charisma modifier additional damage with weapon attacks
  • Divine Sense - grants advantage on attack rolls against fiends
  • Divine Smite - deals an additional 1d8⁠⁠Radiant to fiends
  •  Holy Fire - deals an additional 1d4⁠⁠Radiant per turn to fiends
  • Planar Binding - if successful, takes control of enemy fiend
  • Protection from Evil and Good - fiends have disadvantage against the target
  • Turn the Faithless - turns fiends, causing them to flee
  • Turn the Unholy - turns fiends, causing them to flee
  •  Undead Ward Aura - allied fiends become resistant to ⁠Bludgeoning, ⁠Slashing, and ⁠Piercing damage.

Notes and references

  1. ↑ In traditional D&D lore, Quasits, Succubus and Succubi are demons, which always hail from the Abyss, but in the game, Shovel is simply referred to as a Fiend. Additionally, in the 5e ruleset, Succubus and Succubi are simply fiends, being neither demon nor devil. There is an entry for demons as a race in game data, but it is not used for any creature that exists in the game.
